workload.payloadRule: For group A, B or C and zero-based index i: label = group + "-" + decimal i zero-padded to 4 digits; Data = ((label + "\n").encode("ascii") repeated then truncated to dataBytes); PartitionKey = label. No compression.

observationMethod.frameTiming: Raw frame completion immediately when botocore native generator yields EventStreamMessage, before SDK JSON/base64 decoding. Decode completion also captured. Includes network transfer and local buffering; not server publication time.
observationMethod.wireLength: AWS eventstream prelude total_length includes eventstream headers, payload and 16 framing bytes; excludes TLS and HTTP chunk framing. Payload JSON bytes measured directly. No handcrafted framing or decoder.
observationMethod.termination: Client closes immediately after all preloaded group records are decoded. No natural subscription expiration claim.
observationMethod.cloudWatch: Not queried; no publication wait required.
observationMethod.networkChunkInstrumentation: The attempted raw_stream.stream wrapper observed no chunks: all captured network counters are zero and first/last chunk timestamps null. The SDK event generator had already acquired its source iterator before this wrapper was attached. No first-byte/network-chunk timing claim is made. Raw EventStreamMessage prelude/payload lengths and complete-frame timestamps were captured successfully and are independent of this failed optional instrumentation.

references.fact: Subscriptions last up to 5 minutes; one call per second per consumer/shard; no event payload size limit stated.
Defines Records, ContinuationSequenceNumber, MillisBehindLatest; no event payload size limit stated.
Provisioned shard baseline write 1 MB/sec; GetRecords max 10 MB belongs to GetRecords, not explicitly SubscribeToShard. New large-record support not exercised.
Dedicated enhanced fan-out throughput up to 2 MB/sec per shard per consumer; initial burst formula not documented here.

Record sizing includes raw data plus partition key. Workloads use 655366, 921606 and 499906 total bytes, all strictly below 1 MiB. Native DescribeStreamSummary retained MaxRecordSizeInKiB=1024, PROVISIONED, OpenShardCount=1 and EncryptionType=NONE.

derivedAnalysis.classification: Observed values and explicitly conditional models; raw native responses/decoded frame metadata remain unchanged. Client timing is not server publication timing.

subscriptions.purpose: Discriminate 8,000,000 raw-byte versus 7.5 MiB raw-Data-only / 10 MiB base64-Data-only candidate budgets, on a new owned stream after first stream cleanup. Not a sustained-throughput workload.

observations: Group A repeatedly delivered 12 x 655360-byte records: ten full 7.5 MiB raw-data frames followed by a final 5 MiB frame. Each full frame includes 72 partition-key bytes.
Group B repeatedly delivered 8 x 921600-byte records: twelve 7.03125 MiB raw-data frames, each with 48 partition-key bytes. The first eleven have additional preloaded records available.

A full A frame has 12 separately padded base64 Data strings: 12 * 4 * ceil(655360/3) = 10,485,792 characters, 32 bytes above 10 MiB. Thus strict 10 MiB base64-Data-only, JSON-payload and total-wire caps are all directly contradicted. JSON metadata raises the payload further.

Two record sizes and many backlog frames contradict a greedy-packing 8 MiB or 10 MiB raw-data cap: nine B records would fit below 8 MiB yet native repeatedly delivers only eight. This is evidence against that packing model, not proof those caps cannot coexist with another batching constraint.

Discriminating group C delivered 15,15,10 records of 499900 bytes each. Both first frames have further preloaded records available. A sixteenth would total 7,998,400 raw Data bytes or 7,998,496 with keys, both below 8,000,000. Thus a greedy 8,000,000 raw-data or raw-data-plus-key cap is also contradicted.

conditionalGreedySingleRawDataCapBounds.assumption: All preloaded records available and service greedily includes the next record iff a single raw-data cap permits. Upper bound is conditional, not an unconditional native maximum.

conditionalGreedySingleDataPlusKeyCapBou.assumption: Same model but accounting raw Data plus UTF-8 key bytes.

unresolved: A 7.5 MiB raw-Data-only budget remains compatible, as does an approximate encoded-size budget that ignores per-record base64 padding. Other raw thresholds within the conditional [7,864,320,7,998,400) interval or independent batching constraints remain possible. Group A directly excludes a 7.5 MiB data-plus-key hard cap because its data alone equals 7.5 MiB and it carries 72 extra key bytes. No exact cap is inferred.
No unconditional upper bound or exact native cap established; batching/service-internal constraints are not exposed by these captures.
No claim about large records above the default 1 MiB maximum, compression, higher record counts, different key lengths, consumer reuse, or concurrent-consumer fairness.

observed: Group A first four frames carry 30 MiB; group B first four carry 28.125 MiB. See exact timestamps and all tail windows above.
The first 2 MiB raw-data credit ceiling is contradicted by both first frames, independent of any inferred long-term rate.

Initial observed cumulative delivery exceeds a 2 MiB/s zero-credit envelope. After excluding the first four completed frames, measured remaining-data rates are near 2 MiB/s; all alternative tail windows are retained to expose window sensitivity.
throughputInterpretation.lateWindowSelection: Same explicit rule in both workloads: after completion of frame 4 through completion of last frame. Includes final partial A frame.
throughputInterpretation.interpretation: Compatible with documented dedicated 2 MB/s throughput plus initial/service-side burst allowance. These two ~35-38 second finite reads do not establish an exact steady-state limiter, byte-unit convention, refill rate, token capacity, batching clock or server publication schedule. No literal token-bucket model asserted.
throughputInterpretation.hypotheticalEnvelopeMeaning: Reported minimum startup allowance is max(received raw Data bytes - 2*1048576*client elapsed seconds from response headers). It is a conditional lower bound on initial allowance under that chosen envelope, not an estimate of native configured bucket size; native rate documentation says MB, not explicitly MiB.

reproduction.accountGuard: STS GetCallerIdentity Account equals 000000000000 before CreateStream
steps: Create a unique one-shard PROVISIONED unencrypted-default stream; wait ACTIVE and retain default maximum record size.

For A then B, register a different consumer and wait ACTIVE. Write deterministic records individually at minimum 1.3-second start intervals. Capture every request response and actual before-send event. Abort rather than retry if any write fails.
Wait 15 seconds after group writes. Once only, SubscribeToShard for that group consumer at AT_SEQUENCE_NUMBER of its first record. No later group writes overlap this read.

Iterate SDK EventStream._event_generator. At each yielded SDK EventStreamMessage record prelude.total_length, prelude.headers_length, len(payload), native headers and monotonic/UTC completion time; then call the SDK _parse_event and retain decoded native fields with Data replaced by byteLength and reconstruction metadata.

Close client after all expected records returned, not after 5-minute expiry. Deregister each owned consumer and poll its exact ARN until ResourceNotFoundException; delete owned stream and poll exact name until ResourceNotFoundException.

After first stream cleanup, repeat on a new uniquely owned one-shard provisioned stream and independent reader-C using 40 records of 499900 bytes; same 1.3-second write spacing, 15-second idle, single subscription and cleanup.
reproduction.dataVerification: Probe compared every decoded Data byte string to deterministic reconstructed input and removed every native sequence number from an expected map, asserting the map empty. No hashes or integrity receipts retained.
reproduction.instrumentation: Successful instrumentation: consume SDK _event_generator EventStreamMessage objects, record prelude.total_length, prelude.headers_length, len(payload), completion stamp, then SDK _parse_event and decoded completion stamp. The later attached raw_stream.stream wrapper produced no chunk observations and is not evidence of network chunk sizes/timing. Reproducing first-byte timing would require attaching before SDK response parsing; not needed for captured complete-frame timing.
